rules.fact: No holding the phone; mounted navigation allowed; a single tap or swipe only turns hands-free mode on or off; using apps while driving is banned, including at a red light.
DoorDash: Pause orders. Uber: go offline. Grubhub: 10-minute pause after 2 hours online; repeatedly going unavailable on a block can lead to Schedule Restriction.

Uber Eats Pro: Gold 30%, Platinum 50% acceptance (Boston). DoorDash Dasher Rewards: thresholds by area (NYC 65-85%). Grubhub levels: offer commitment 80% / 95%. Perks include priority for better-paying orders.
At most one decline or unassign per hour; a second ends the Earn by Time dash. Availability in Boston not published.
All three allow working for other apps; each requires timely delivery; DoorDash lists failing to deliver in a timely manner as a deactivation reason; Grubhub warns about late orders.
Uber advises against accepting orders on both apps at once; Grubhub allows it if the Grubhub order is not delayed; lateness can cost account access.

rules.topic: Acceptance and how common multi-apping is
rules.fact: NYC 2021: 56% of delivery workers used more than one app; about 36% of offers accepted while waiting (one in every ~11 minutes vs an offer every ~4).

s21.note: One report, central Massachusetts, before costs; a check, not a fit.

method.note: Offers from each app arrive independently while you wait. A typical one-app driver takes the better half of offers; that reproduces each app's single-app wait. With several apps you catch most offers (85-100%), lose about a minute per order pausing the others, and take an offer when its pay beats your average earnings per minute over its minutes. Kept pay = pay - gas - 30% x (pay - 72.5 cents x miles), as on the app cards. Stacking (a second app's order added to the trip you are on) is a worked case from stated assumptions; account risk is not priced.
method.stacking: compatible share 15-35% of other apps' offers, 8-14 extra minutes, 5-30% of tips lost on both orders
